c.tagline: Japan's best-preserved castle town — a legendary garden, gold leaf, and geisha teahouse streets.

taxi.fareNote: Ride-hailing apps (GO, Uber) only dispatch licensed metered taxis rather than private cars, and coverage is thinner than in Tokyo or Osaka — flagging a metered taxi at a rank or by phone is often quickest. The Kanazawa Loop Bus covers most sightseeing.

avoid.reason: Katamachi's nightlife strip has occasional bar touts late at night; otherwise just usual awareness.

hood_desc: The transport hub around JR Kanazawa Station and its dramatic wooden Tsuzumi Gate, where the Hokuriku Shinkansen from Tokyo arrives; ringed by hotels, department stores and the Loop Bus terminal. The most convenient base for first-timers who want maximum connectivity.

Kanazawa's main downtown for shopping, dining and nightlife — Korinbo's department stores flow into Katamachi's dense grid of izakaya, bars and clubs along the Sai River. Walkable to Omicho Market, the 21st Century Museum and Kenroku-en, and the go-to area for going out.

The largest and most atmospheric of Kanazawa's three geisha teahouse districts, a preserved lattice-fronted quarter of wooden chaya, gold-leaf shops, tea salons and traditional ryokan. The most beautiful, culture-steeped place to stay in old Japan.

The historic and cultural core around Kanazawa Castle Park and Kenroku-en, one of Japan's three great gardens, alongside the 21st Century Museum of Contemporary Art and Oyama Shrine. Ideal for sightseeing at a calm, green pace.

A remarkably intact samurai residential quarter of earthen walls, private canals and gardens, with the Nomura family house and craft workshops. A quiet, atmospheric base a short walk from Korinbo's shops and restaurants.
lodging: OMO5 Kanazawa Katamachi by Hoshino Resorts

water.note: Tap water is safe and good quality.

transit.pay: Tap a nationwide Suica/ICOCA IC card or the local ICa card, or pay cash on board; a flat city-bus fare is around ¥200 (~$1.35). A one-day Loop Bus / city-bus pass (about ¥600) covers most sightseeing and is the best value for a day of touring.
transit.hours: Loop and city buses run roughly 8:00am to 6:00pm (a limited Light-Up Bus adds evening runs to key sights); after the buses stop, taxis fill the gap.
transit.note: Kanazawa has no subway or tram — the clockwise/counter-clockwise Kanazawa Loop Bus and the wider Hokutetsu bus network are the main way to reach the sights, and the compact center is very walkable.

bus: Highway buses to Tokyo, Nagoya, Osaka & Kyoto

transit.m: Hokutetsu limousine bus to Kanazawa Station West Gate (~40-45 min, hourly)
Airport shuttle bus to JR Komatsu Station, then IR Ishikawa Line or Shinkansen to Kanazawa

tip.r: Not customary; tipping is not expected anywhere in Japan and can cause confusion.
